subject: cube planet
title: What If the Earth Were a Cube? You'd Live in Six Round Puddles

scenes.text: What if Earth were a cube? Every ocean would gather into six round puddles.
Gravity still pulls toward the centre. The cube is about 10,000 kilometres wide, and the middle of each face sits closest to the core.
Air and water slide downhill to those centres. The atmosphere is about 100 kilometres thick. The corners stick out 3,700 kilometres farther than the faces.
So each face holds one round sea and a ring of land. The edges and corners rise naked into the vacuum of space.
Walk toward an edge and flat ground feels like a steepening mountain, because gravity leans back toward the centre. You'd weigh less at the corners.
Six separate worlds, cut off by airless rock. Until gravity won, and slowly crushed the cube back into a ball.

description:
What if Earth were a cube? Gravity would still point toward the planet's centre, so a cube with Earth's volume, roughly 10,000 kilometres on a side, would have its lowest ground at the centre of each face. Air and water would flow there, forming six round seas ringed by land, while the edges and corners, about 3,700 kilometres farther from the core than the face centres and far above the 100-kilometre-thick atmosphere, would stand in vacuum.
Walking toward an edge would feel like climbing a steepening slope even on flat ground, and you would weigh less at the corners. Each face would be an isolated world with its own weather, and over time gravity would pull the whole thing back into a sphere.

first_comment: Any rocky body more than a few hundred kilometres across gets squeezed round by its own gravity, which is why every planet is a ball. Which shape would you give Earth if you could?
